sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Both opinions are true because they have their root in the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof, which contains two aspects: being infinitely above and infinitely below.

translations.translation: And it is explained in the discourses,
that both opinions are true,
for both have their root in the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof,
for in Ein Sof there are two matters.
That He is above, above, without end,
and that He is below, below, without limit.
And these two matters are the root of the lower knowledge and the higher knowledge.
For from the aspect of the revelation of Ein Sof,
which is revealed in every place below, below without limit,
everything before Him is considered as nothing — this is the higher knowledge that "below there is nothing."
And from the aspect of the concealment of Ein Sof,
which is elevated in His Awtsmoos above, above without end,
the creations exist as a tangible entity — this is the lower knowledge that "below there is something."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: It must be understood how the lower knowledge, rooted in the concealment of Ein Sof, is perfected by the revelation of the higher knowledge, and why it is still considered true.

translations.translation: And one must understand,
that since even the lower knowledge has its root in the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof,
the perfection of the lower knowledge would seemingly be that within it there should be a revelation that "below there is something"
(not that the creations are a tangible entity from their own perspective,
but rather)
because Ein Sof is above, above without end,
and in the discourses it is explained,
that the perfection of the lower knowledge comes about through the revelation of the higher knowledge shining within it.
Also, one must understand on the other hand,
regarding what is said in the discourses that even the lower knowledge is true because it has a root in the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof,
for seemingly,
since the matter of "above, above without end"
(the root of the lower knowledge)
is the concealment of Ein Sof,
the perception that "below there is something"
(as is perceived in the lower knowledge)
is seemingly not from the aspect of Ein Sof, but rather on the contrary,
because Ein Sof is not perceived within it,
and nevertheless they say,
that the opinion that "below there is something"
(as it is in the lower knowledge)
is a true opinion.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The explanation of the term "nature" is discussed, with several interpretations: that it is a new name for constant miracles, that it derives from the word for a coin stamp, or that it refers to something without reason or intellect.

translations.translation: And the explanation is,
that it is explained in the discourses,
that the term "nature" has several interpretations.
For in the Responsa of the Chacham Tzvi
it is stated,
that the name "nature" is a new term coined by the later sages.
For since everything
(even nature)
is from Him, blessed be He,
therefore even nature is a miracle.
Except that these miracles are constant,
continuous miracles.
And there are those who say
that "nature" (teva) is from the word "coin" (matbea).
For it is stated in the Mishnah,
A person strikes many coins with one seal, and they all resemble one another,
but the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, stamped every person with the seal of Adam the first man, yet not one of them resembles another.
And in the Tanya
it is stated,
that "nature" is a borrowed term for anything that is not according to reason and intellect.
